# Two capability questions and their first hard operations

This is new work by the same sole Sol worker. The three completed Gaussian-memory stages and the former Ultra's research are preserved. No achievement of the civilisation-scale mission is claimed here.

## Can one physical-count reservoir stabilize arbitrary conservative weakly reversible kinetics?

The proposed foundational question concerns a finite raw mass-action reaction list with positive rational rates and a positive conservation vector. Add only `0 <-> A`. Does every closed communication class have a stationary probability, and what actual-count tails and return-time properties can be acquired without a stationary-fiber, mixing or boundary-service oracle? Full success would supply a general structural stability principle across arbitrary coupled stoichiometric geometry, rather than an extra recognized architecture. It would also clarify the relation to the general positive-recurrence conjecture through conservative homogenization; passage to an infinite-rate chemostat would need its own uniform-tightness proof.

The former Ultra's completed source N1628 already handles arbitrary finite shared-port compositions of disjoint nonport rank-one blocks, and proves that every scalar port-only multiplier fails on a coupled cubic example. N1612 is the accepted full-graph small-tilt successor for its specified binary one-port hub/arm architecture, with genuine multiface transfer. Neither is an arbitrary-rank theorem. Their actual costs and acceptance boundaries remain unchanged.

The first new hard attack tests a stronger property before trying to extend it. The exact family

    B+C_j <-> C_(j+1), j=0,...,m-1,
    A+C_0 <-> B+C_0,
    0 <-> A,
    sum_j C_j=1,

is binary, reversible and conservative before the sole reservoir is added. With unit rates its ordinary detailed-balance stationary law has independent Poisson(1) A and B and a uniform enzyme phase. Nevertheless its L2 spectral gap is ZERO for every m>=2: the high-inventory cut `B+j>=n` has conductance at most `n/[n(n-1)...(n-m+1)]`. This rules out silently replacing actual-time return geometry by a uniform spectral gap. It does not refute positive recurrence or exponential stationary tails, which this example has and the strongest ordinary construction already supplies.
